Article Title: 'We're nowhere near favourites': France's Maxime Vachier-Lagrave says India not the only Chess Olympiad contender
Article Text:
Maxime Vachier-Lagrave names India among Chess Olympiad contenders

Chess began as a hobby for MVL

Maxime Vachier-Lagrave at 2024 Chess Olympiad (Photo by FIDE)

The MVL philosophy

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Every time I come to India, in the morning I feel very tired, no matter how I slept. Maxime Vachier-Lagrave, French Grandmaster

ALSO READ:

NEW DELHI: The 46th edition of the Chess Olympiad kicked off in style for the French men's team on Wednesday as they secured a clean 4-0 sweep over lower-ranked Tunisia. Maxime Vachier-Lagrave, popularly known as MVL, was absent from action as the Board 1 player was rested, perhaps much needed after a gruelling week of matches in India's Global Chess League (GCL).This time, France's team enters the fray with a solid side featuring MVL, Étienne Bacrot, Maxime Lagarde, Jules Moussard and youngester Marc'Andria Maurizzi. Sébastien Mazé serves as captain.But ask MVL whether France can win the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, and he does not reach for a diplomatic hedge, a motivational cliché or the line about how anything can happen in a Swiss system."We're nowhere near favourites," he told TimesofIndia.com during an exclusive interaction. "But we have a good solid team, and I think everyone's really motivated. So that's all I can say, and we're hoping for the best."Then, who are the favourites in his opinion?"There are three main favourites, I think. Even four, I would say. USA, India, China and Uzbekistan," the French grandmaster added.Four teams named without hesitation, France not among them, by the man who will be leading France from its top board.This is not pessimism. Spend twenty minutes with MVL, and it becomes clear that it is something closer to the opposite.He possesses a settled, unsentimental clarity about what he can control and what he cannot, precisely the mindset that has kept him at the sport's summit for the better part of two decades."I learned the rules at five years old, and gradually I enjoyed the game more and more and started winning," MVL recalled. "This is always, as a kid, the way you kind of pick up a hobby or passion. The more you win, the more you want to play."What he did not anticipate was permanence."I didn't know at the time that I would still be doing basically only that as my profession thirty years later," he continued. "But here we are, and hopefully I've got a few good years remaining."Even when discussing his own longevity, the 35-year-old declines to overclaim. He is careful, too, not to romanticise the profession, even as he defends the choice that led him into what he now calls "a great decision"."Overall I have it easier, because of course it's something I profoundly love since my childhood," he told this website. "But of course, as every profession, it has some moments of doubt, some moments that are not so easy. I think I made a great decision twenty years back."Along the way, there have been setbacks, but he has learnt to put them aside."For everyone, every sportsman, every chess player, there are moments of doubt, moments where things don't go so well. It's just important not to focus on those moments. But to learn the lessons that need to be learned, and to focus on the moments of enjoyment," he said."An improvement curve cannot be a straight line. It has some ups and downs. You just need to always be looking forwards for the ups."Over the past fortnight, MVL had a good time in India, playing for Mumba Masters, who finished fourth in Season 4 of the GCL, although there has not been much sightseeing for him, why?"Every time I come to India, in the morning I feel very tired, no matter how I slept," he admitted, a little apologetically.Besides chess, little sightseeing and tired mornings in India, he found friends who would wake up late to play board games with him, as well as physical sports such as padel during his free time. When he is alone and has some time to himself, his downtime runs to variant sudoku.In Samarkand, he'll sit on Board 1 for a team he has already told you isn't among the favourites, and then, presumably, play as though nobody had mentioned it.
Article Summary: Maxime Vachier-Lagrave, popularly known as MVL, will lead France in the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand. The 35-year-old has been at the top of the game for the better part of two decades. He says India, USA, China and Uzbekistan are among the favourites to win.

Article Title: From torrential rain to typhoon threat: Asian Games face turbulent start in Aichi-Nagoya
Article Text:
Signages of the 20th Asian Games on display in Nagoya, central Japan. (Reuters Photo)

Heavy rain has already disrupted Games

ALSO READ:

China’s cricket campaign ends without a ball

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya are facing an early weather threat, with organisers bracing for possible disruption from a tropical storm that could strengthen into a typhoon and approach central Japan just as the continental multi-sport event gets into full swing.The 20th Asian Games officially open with the opening ceremony in Nagoya on Saturday, but several competitions have already begun, including football, basketball, volleyball and cricket. The Games are scheduled to run from September 19 to October 4, with 43 sports on the programme.Tropical Storm Dujuan was located off Japan's Pacific coast early Thursday and was moving northwest towards central Japan, where Nagoya is located. The storm had maximum sustained winds of 90 kmph, with gusts reaching 126 kmph. Forecasts were raising the possibility of the system approaching the Aichi-Nagoya region around Monday.The weather threat comes after torrential rain battered Nagoya and surrounding areas last week, disrupting transport and forcing several hundred athletes to evacuate their accommodation.Kosei Inoue, Japan's chef de mission for the Games and a senior executive board member of the Japanese Olympic Committee, acknowledged the possibility of further disruption at a news conference on Thursday."Due to the heavy rain and severe weather, some competitions have already experienced delays or postponements, and there is also a possibility that a typhoon could approach on September 21," Inoue said."Under these circumstances, we are holding thorough meetings within the JOC to ensure that we are fully prepared and capable of responding appropriately to these situations."The possibility of another major weather system adds to the logistical challenge facing organisers, who are already managing an unusually large Games involving around 17,000 athletes and officials.The impact of the weather was already evident in the women's cricket competition on Thursday. Bangladesh advanced to the semi-finals after their quarter-final against China was abandoned because of a wet outfield at Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin, with the match called off without even a toss taking place.Bangladesh, ranked 10th in the ICC women's T20I rankings, progressed over China, who are ranked 36th, under the competition's washout provisions. Bangladesh will face the winner of Friday's quarter-final between defending champions India and Japan in the semi-finals on September 20.The abandoned cricket match was an early reminder of how vulnerable outdoor events can be to weather conditions during the Games. With the possibility of a typhoon approaching the region on September 21, organisers now face the prospect of managing further disruptions just as the Asian Games move into their opening week.
Article Summary: Tropical Storm Dujuan was located off Japan's Pacific coast early Thursday and was moving northwest towards central Japan. The storm had maximum sustained winds of 90 kmph, with gusts reaching 126 kmph. Forecasts were raising the possibility of the system approaching the Aichi-Nagoya region around Monday.

Article Title: Chess Olympiad: How India's Arjun Erigaisi suffered biggest Round 1 upset against lower-rated opponent
Article Text:
Arjun Erigaisi at FIDE Chess Olympiad 2026 Round 1 (Photo by Rafal Oleksiewicz for FIDE)

How Arjun lost the plot

India earn convincing wins in both categories

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Arjun Erigaisi (rated 2759) is India's second-ranked chess player at the moment. On Wednesday, with R Praggnanandhaa, India's current No. 1, rested, the 23-year-old Telangana grandmaster took Board 1 for India at the 2026 Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan.India's opposition was Thailand, whose top board was occupied by 2363-rated International Master Prin Laohawirapap, the Thai No. 1. With a rating gap of almost 400 Elo points, and Arjun holding the white pieces, the result looked a formality.Instead, it became one of the biggest Round 1 upsets in Olympiad history. Chess.com even made the Thai IM's win over Arjun its Game of the Day, with only Iraqi CM Ali Ehsan Aryan's draw against Levon Aronian coming close as an upset against a 2700-rated grandmaster."The Indian grandmaster playing white started the game with the Colle system, which is not necessarily one of the sharpest systems. He got a slight advantage from the position," veteran Grandmaster Pravin Thipsay told TimesofIndia.com while analysing the game.The first real opening came on move 18."The Thai player made a serious error of judgement by playing Rook e8. Instead of the 18th move, black taking on f5, e into f5, would have led to equality.But after Rook e8, Arjun was in a very powerful position," he assessed.At that stage, Thipsay noted, the win looked routine as Arjun was gaining considerable time advantage on the clock as well. However, it was move 28 that changed things."Instead of launching a pawn roller with h4 on the 28th move, Arjun chose to trade the black knight which had come to his territory, and Bxd3 turned out to be a mistake which led to an equal position," the grandmaster told this website.Thailand's Prin then returned the favour."On the 31st move, now it was the Thailand player who made a serious mistake," Thipsay said. "He could have probably equalised. There is no direct kingside attack coming. The move chosen by the Thailand player was really very dangerous. It weakened his kingside, and Arjun was in a completely winning position thereafter."What followed was a masterclass in resourcefulness from the lower-rated player."The Thai player really played resourcefully and was successful in complicating the game. The Thai player offered a rook, an exchange as we call it, rook for knight, on move 46-47," he explained."By taking the rook, knight into e4 on move 47, Arjun could have won the game. Though his king was very exposed, and it might have led to a perpetual check or something else. But yes, white had a decisive advantage with accurate play had he taken the rook with knight into e4. Instead, he played knight f3, not taking the rook, which led to a drawish position."Even then, the half point was there. It was ambition that cost him."In the drawish position, again at move 50, Arjun played the ambitious move Qg7, trying to checkmate the opponent, which allowed a very basic checkmate to black. By playing the 50th move Qf4, Arjun could have defended himself and the game would have ended in a draw. But after the move played, Qg7, he got checkmated very fast," Thipsay added."Quite an unexpected result considering the difference of around 400 rating points, a great setback for Arjun."Arjun Erigaisi's defeat, however, did not affect India's overall team score. Gukesh, Nihal Sarin, and Vidit Gujrathi all defeated their opponents, helping India seal a 3–1 team victory.The Indian women's team, with Divya Deshmukh rested, produced an even more dominant performance, defeating the Dominican Republic 4–0.India was among nine of the top 10 seeds to record clean sweeps on the opening day of the Women's Olympiad. Germany was the only team among the top 10 seeds to drop a game, narrowly defeating Malta 3–1.India, defending champions in both sections, play Indonesia in the Open on Thursday, while the women's team takes on Finland.
Article Summary: Arjun Erigaisi (rated 2759) is India's second-ranked chess player at the moment. 23-year-old Telangana grandmaster took Board 1 for India at the 2026 Chess Olympiad. India's opposition was Thailand, whose top board was occupied by 2363-rated International Master Prin Laohawirapap, the Thai No. 1.

Article Title: Women boxers will corner the glory at Asian Games: Vijender Singh
Article Text:
L-R: Lovlina Borgohain, Jaismine Lamboria, Priya Ghanghas, Preeti Pawar, Sakshi Chaudhary and Arundhati Choudhary at the CWG 2026 in Glasgow. (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The gloves have barely cooled after India’s record-breaking 2026 Commonwealth Games campaign, but Vijender Singh knows the real examination begins now.As India heads to AichiNagoya, the former Olympic and World Championships bronze medallist sounded a note of caution.“In comparison with the Commonwealth Games, the Asian Games will be tough for our boxers. They’re in good form, doing great but Asian Games will be different and far more difficult,” Vijender told TOI.His assessment comes at a particularly interesting moment. Indian boxing returned from Glasgow with seven gold medals and three silver — its best-ever haul at a Commonwealth Games. Among those who climbed to the top of the podium were Sachin Siwach, Sakshi Chaudhary, Preeti Pawar and Priya Ghanghas, three of whom Vijender identified as key medal hopes for Aichi-Nagoya.The challenge is that the Asian ring brings a different kind of pressure. China, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan and Japan have traditionally provided some of the continent’s deepest boxing strength, with several of their fighters also operating at the Olympic level. Yet, Vijender expects India to return with a healthy medal haul, though he sees the women leading the charge.“I think our boxers can get three to four medals from the Asian Games.Let’s say, I’m expecting two-three from the girls and one or two medals can be clinched by the boys too.”His confidence in the women is understandable. Sakshi, Preeti and Priya arrive in Aichi-Nagoya after gold-medal performances in Glasgow.“Among the men, Sachin (Siwach) is a strong medal hope for India. Then there is (Narender) Berwal, who won bronze at the 2022 Asian Games. He also won the Arjuna award recently.“But my favourites are the girls. There is Sakshi (Chaudhary), Preeti (Pawar), who are strong contenders, and I also think that Priya Ghanghas is going to perform really well at the Asian Games. Coaches, trainers, who I’ve spoken to, have been raving about these three women boxers,” Vijender said.Siwach and Berwal, too, will go to Aichi-Nagoya with fresh evidence of their rising credentials. Siwach won the 60kg gold in Glasgow, while Berwal took silver in the 90kg plus category.
Article Summary: Vijender Singh says Asian Games will be more difficult for Indian boxers. Indian boxing returned from Glasgow with seven gold medals and three silver. Sachin Siwach, Sakshi Chaudhary, Preeti Pawar and Priya Ghanghas are key medal hopes.

Article Title: Asian Games: NADA panel’s interim order gives Abhishek Pal reprieve
Article Text:
Abhishek Pal

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: Long-distance runner Abhishek Pal’s hopes of competing at the Asian Games received a big boost after the Anti-Doping Disciplinary Panel of National Anti-Doping Agency clarified that there is no suspension that prevents the athlete from competing. Pal won the 10,000m gold and 5,000m silver at the inter-state meet in June but Athletics Federation of India (AFI) dropped him from the Asiad squad, citing adverse analytical findings in a National AntiDoping Agency (NADA) report.Hearing Pal’s appeal, the panel refused to quash the Notice of Charge but ordered a final hearing within four weeks. “No provisional suspension has been imposed on the athlete. The status quo as of today shall be maintained until the final disposal of this case,” the panel said in its interim order on Tuesday. The panel noted that “the athlete is not suspended and may continue to participate in competitions, subject to the final outcome of these proceedings. ”In its observations and findings, the panel stated that “the athlete’s follow-up doping control tests conducted on June 7, June 21 and June 24 have all returned negative . The athlete’s previous test on May 6 was also negative. The athlete has been tested about 20 times and all results are negative.These are relevant circumstances to be considered at the final hearing.”NADA argued that it does not want to send a dope-tainted athlete to the Games. The sample collected on May 10, during the Indian Athletics Series 2 in Chennai, returned an Atypical Finding (ATF) for clomifene. The estimated concentration was reported as 0.032 ng/mL, which is below the Minimum Reporting Level (MRL) of 2.0 ng/mL specified by World AntiDoping Agency (WADA).NDTL suggested an investigation to explain the ATF. Following an investigation, NADA issued a decision on Aug 14, classifying the ATF as an Adverse Analytical Finding (AAF). A notice proposing a two-year period of ineligibility was issued on Sept 2. “I’m hopeful of competing at the Asiad,” Pal, who was represented by Parth Goswami and Niharika Tiwari, told TOI.Meanwhile, AFI sources said, “Based on the NADA panel’s interim directions, AFI will again discuss Pal’s case. No one else (other than Gulveer Singh) has qualified in the men’s 5,000m and 10,000m,” they added. Pal clocked 13:33.95s in Belgium in May to meet the AFI’s qualification mark of 13:39.18s in the men’s 5000m.
Article Summary: Long-distance runner Abhishek Pal's hopes of competing at the Asian Games received a big boost. The Anti-Doping Disciplinary Panel of National Anti- Doping Agency clarified that there is no suspension that prevents the athlete from competing. The panel refused to quash the Notice of Charge but ordered a final hearing within four weeks.

Article Title: Asian Games: Hurdler Nandhini came close to quitting, but never gave up
Article Text:
K Nandhini

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

CHENNAI: There was a time when 100m hurdler K Nandini and national-record holder Jyothi Yarraji would often trade places on the podium in age-group categories. While Jyothi found the right guidance and surged ahead, Tamil Nadu’s Nandhini struggled, eventually forcing her to quit athletics for nearly four months in 2023.Three years later, the 27-year-old is headed to the Asian Games after rebuilding her career. She clocked a personal best of 13.22 seconds at the Inter-State meet in June to breach the Asiad qualifying mark and followed it up by finishing on top at the recent Indian Athletics Series Final.“I have been waiting for this opportunity for a long time. Like I approach other competitions, I will approach the Asian Games in the same way and not put myself under pressure. The aim is to clock below 13 seconds, and I am able to do that in training,” Nandhini told TOI.She had to train on her own for three years after her coach, Nagarajan, with whom she had trained for nearly a decade, left due to personal reasons. She was in search of a coach but could not find one who could take her to the next stage before joining hands with Pradeep from Sports Development Authority of Tamil Nadu (SDAT).“Training alone, it was hard to motivate myself. It was during this period that I quit sports and started preparing for the Income Tax exam.I took the decision because I felt like I was wasting time and that age was catching up. In between, I received a call letter for Income Tax recruitment through the sports quota, and they asked me to come for trials. I did not want to let this opportunity go, so I slowly started training again. But I could not make it.“I deliberately did not attend many competitions because I knew I would not perform well. Coach Pradeep had good knowledge and was working elsewhere. I was waiting to train under him, but his appointment at the SDAT was delayed. Once we got together, we did not try to improve my timings quickly because my technique was poor and I was mentally very weak. He understood what I needed. I did not win any medal for eight months but believed in the process. While I could not medal, I kept improving my timings slowly.”
Article Summary: K Nandini will compete in the 100m hurdles at the Asian Games. The 27-year-old had to train on her own for three years after her coach left due to personal reasons. She clocked a personal best of 13.22 seconds at the Inter-State meet in June.

Article Title: Gukesh on Board 4: Top-board gold medallist in last two Olympiads faces new challenge
Article Text:
D Gukesh (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Defending champions and top seeds Team India have sprang a big surprise even though it’s backed by current form and rating logic. Whether that was needed or would necessarily hamper the planning of their chief Olympiad rivals is the big question.D Gukesh, who had amassed 18 points in 21 games and two individual gold medals on the top board in the last two editions, has been assigned to play on the fourth board in the biennial team event at Samarkand, Uzbekistan, that began on Wednesday. R Praggnanandhaa (2761), Arjun Erigaisi (2759) and Nihal Sarin (2718) will play on the top three boards.Some surprise element was expected in India’s board order as captain N Srinath did not reveal his cards till 11pm on Tuesday night.To get designated on the fourth board is an unprecedented situation for the reigning world champion (Gukesh) in the history of Olympiad. But then Gukesh has an intense relationship with the unprecedented - becoming the classical matchplay world champion at age 18 and then slipping to Elo 2702 and outside world’s top-30 two years later. That included some wooden spoons in elite events too.Thankfully, Gukesh and the inform Praggnanandhaa, who skipped the exhibition-like GCL in Bengaluru that ended on Sunday, have got more rest than the majority of other elite players.Pragg on the top board is an interesting prospect too.It is unclear if India arrived at the board order as a strategy - to play Arjun in the top half and Gukesh in the bottom half (very different from the last Olympiad) - or, if the players and captain Srinath failed to reach a consensus and followed the Elo rating sequence. “No comments on the board order now,” Srinath told TOI. “Team is motivated and upbeat. Delay in getting rooms was quite unfair and upsetting. But it’s behind us and we will focus on chess now. ”Two years ago, Srinath was more than ready to explain his decision to demote Arjun to the third board and promote Pragg to the second. Seven-time Olympian Praveen Thipsay said, “If I was playing a strong tournament or a strong match that Gukesh is playing (World Championship against Sindarov in Geneva from Nov 24), I would prefer my preceding tournament (to be) against stronger opponents so that I am ready for the big challenge ahead.“But my personality may not be like that of Gukesh. In the present scenario (playing on board 4), even if Gukesh scores successive wins in the initial five-six rounds, more than the wins, the manner of his wins and quality of play will determine if he regains the valuable confidence or not."
Article Summary: Defending champions and top seeds Team India have sprang a big surprise. D Gukesh has been assigned to play on the fourth board in the biennial team event at Samarkand, Uzbekistan. R Praggnanandhaa (2761), Arjun Erigaisi (2759) and Nihal Sarin (2718) will play on top three boards.

Article Title: How China’s Asian Games cricket campaign ended without a ball being bowled as Bangladesh advanced to the semis
Article Text:
File Pic: Chinese women's cricket team (Getty Images)

Rain ends China’s campaign before it begins

Bangladesh team (Getty Images)

Bangladesh eye another medal challenge

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

China’s women’s cricket campaign at the Asian Games ended in agonising fashion on Thursday, without the team even taking the field, as their quarter-final against Bangladesh was abandoned without a ball being bowled because of a wet outfield in Nisshin, Aichi prefecture.The T20 match at Korogi Sports Park was called off without the toss taking place after persistent rain and poor weather conditions made play impossible. With no result possible, Bangladesh advanced to the semi-finals on the basis of their higher international ranking, bringing China’s third Asian Games cricket appearance since 2010 to an abrupt end.Bangladesh are ranked 10th in the ICC Women’s T20I rankings, while China are 36th. Under the Asian Games cricket Playing Conditions, the higher-ranked side advances if a quarter-final is abandoned without a result. The same provision was used at the 2023 Asian Games in Hangzhou, where three of the four women’s quarter-finals involving India, Pakistan and Bangladesh were washed out.For China, the outcome was particularly frustrating after making it through to the knockout stage of the eight-team women’s competition.The side had hoped to make an impact on the continental stage but instead saw its campaign end without facing a single delivery in the quarter-final.Heavy weather had affected the Korogi Sports Park area throughout the week, and conditions deteriorated enough on Thursday to force a complete cancellation of play. The venue on the outskirts of Nagoya is hosting all the cricket matches at the Asian Games.Bangladesh, meanwhile, moved into the last four without having to bat or bowl. Nigar Sultana’s side will now face the winner of Friday’s quarter-final between defending champions India and hosts Japan in the semi-finals on September 20.India, led by Harmanpreet Kaur, will begin their title defence against Japan in Nisshin on Friday. The other quarter-final on Thursday pits Pakistan against Thailand at the same venue.With only eight teams featuring in the women’s cricket competition, Bangladesh are now just one victory away from reaching the gold-medal match. Both semi-finals are scheduled for September 20, with the gold-medal match to be played on September 22.Bangladesh’s progression also highlights the importance of the tournament regulations in a weather-hit competition. Rather than using a reserve day for the quarter-final, the Playing Conditions provide for the higher-ranked side to progress when a match is completely washed out.China’s exit means the country’s Asian Games cricket campaign is now over. The Chinese men’s side was not included in the eight-team field, leaving the women’s team as the country’s sole representative in cricket at Aichi-Nagoya 2026.The Games have started several sporting competitions before the official opening ceremony, and cricket is among the events beginning ahead of Saturday’s ceremony.The Asian Games cricket competition will conclude with the women’s final on September 22. On the same day, India’s men’s team, led by Shreyas Iyer , are scheduled to play Japan in a T20I at the Sano International Cricket Ground, around 100km from Tokyo. The match is part of celebrations marking 75 years of diplomatic relations between India and Japan.
Article Summary: China's women's cricket campaign at the Asian Games ended in agonising fashion on Thursday, without the team even taking the field. Their quarter-final against Bangladesh was abandoned without a ball being bowled because of a wet outfield in Nisshin, Aichi prefecture. With no result possible, Bangladesh advanced to the semi-finals on the basis of their higher international ranking. The Asian Games cricket competition will conclude with the women’s final on September 22.

Article Title: ‘Funds insufficient’: Indian equestrian riders forced to pay for hay, bedding and fodder ahead of Asian Games
Article Text:
Representative image: Indian equestrian (X Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Indian equestrian riders preparing for the Asian Games have been left to arrange hay, bedding and fodder for their horse combinations, with the Indian Olympic Association (IOA)-appointed ad-hoc committee running the sport citing a shortage of govt funds.The financial strain has added to the riders’ burden at a crucial stage of their preparations, forcing them to source essential feed from stores and stables and pay from their own pockets.A mail accessed by TOI, signed by Lt Col Sandeep Dewan, member (administration), ad-hoc committee and team leader of the equestrian contingent, states that funds released by the govt to the national federation have been insufficient even to clear the bill of transporter Peden Bloodstock. The federation, the mail adds, has covered the shortfall from its own funds.“We regret to inform you that the government has so far not released any funds for payment of feed and other expenses related to the maintenance of the horses whilst in Japan,” Dewan wrote.The riders have been asked to purchase hay, bedding and other stable requirements directly and claim reimbursement from the federation, which will subsequently seek govt clearance and payment.The financial uncertainty extends beyond Japan. Riders told TOI that they had personally borne expenses for food, travel, accommodation and quarantine fees during their horses’ mandatory quarantine in Aachen, Germany.Reimbursements for pre-quarantine tests, blood and swab tests, horse transportation, athlete accommodation and groom accommodation also remain pending.“Timely support on these essential matters is extremely important for us to focus completely on our performance,” a rider said. For a contingent preparing to represent India at the continental stage, the unresolved payments have become an unwelcome distraction from the sporting challenge ahead.
Article Summary: Indian equestrian riders left to arrange hay, bedding and fodder for their horse combinations. Indian Olympic Association (IOA)-appointed ad-hoc committee running the sport cites a shortage of govt funds. Financial strain has added to the riders’ burden at a crucial stage of their preparations.

Article Title: 'I'm done playing the victim': Sumit Nagal reveals 'change' in mindset after difficult 2026
Article Text:
Sumit Nagal of Team India (Photo by Abhishek Chinnappa/Getty Images for ITF)

Nagal changes his approach

'The focus right now is to compete’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India’s top-ranked singles player Sumit Nagal has had a difficult 2026 season, with injuries disrupting his progress and pushing him down to No. 247 in the rankings. But the 29-year-old says he has changed his mindset and is now focused more on enjoying tennis than constantly worrying about results.Nagal started the year with a hip injury picked up during a Challenger event in Thailand. He returned early for India’s Davis Cup tie against the Netherlands in Bengaluru because he wanted to represent the country."I started the year with an injury, then played Davis Cup (in Bengaluru). I was always running behind time. I came in early to play because it was Davis Cup and Team India," Nagal told PTI."If it wasn't for the Davis Cup, I would have taken the whole month off.”He later developed a wrist problem and said he did not feel fully fit until May."I was in a position where I wasn't healthy, but I was playing. And then March, again, I started feeling something in my wrist. So I didn't feel good till I would say May."Despite the setbacks, Nagal won a Challenger title in Romania and reached another semifinal in Czechia. He believes his game has improved in recent months.“The last two, three months have been better comparing to the first half of the year.And now I just have to build on it," he said.His US Open qualifying campaign ended with a 3-6, 6-7(4) loss to France’s Arthur Gea. Nagal, however, felt the close match showed he can still compete at a high level."My last match in the US Open was a little bit unfortunate. I had a few break points and the guy ended up making the fourth round. So I feel like it's there, it's just I need to work hard for it to go in my favour," he said.The constant cycle of playing and recovering also affected him mentally."It's not so fun, because when you play for two months and then you're out for two months and you play for two months, I don't think it's so much fun. But I'm done playing the victim. I take it as what it is, how it is, and I try to enjoy every day.Before the US Open, Nagal realised he needed to stop putting all his focus on winning."I realised that I need to be more happy. Very simple, actually. And not focus too much about winning, winning, winning, winning. Because I was doing that and it wasn't really working for me."A loss to Jan Kumsat in Prague helped him reach that realisation."I lost a match in Prague and I was driving back. And that's when I realised, I said, man, like this is just not fun. I'm not going to survive like this if I keep putting pressure on myself that every match I step on, I need to win, win, win,” Nagal said."I was just burning too much energy throughout the match and throughout the days."Nagal has also put his immediate goal of returning to the top 100 aside."You always want to play the Slams. You want to be top 50, top 30. But I wouldn't say that's my focus right now. The focus right now is to compete, man," he said.Earlier in the season, he often struggled to maintain his level throughout matches."For a lot of weeks, I was playing two good sets and not the third set. That's very basic. Or I was playing one good set and not a good second set because I was just playing the victim thing and saying, ‘Oh, this is not working for myself. This is not working. This is against me. Everything was against me’," he said.“And like this, whatever, you can have any goals. But like this, you're not going to reach anywhere.”Nagal is also willing to help younger Indian players but does not want to force himself into a leadership role.“I'm always open for them. I guide them if something is needed. But also, I don't want to be in there, let's say, as a leadership role when it's not asked,” he said.“At the end of the day, it's still a team sport. It shouldn't be one guy leading the team. Of course, my help is there. I've always said it. I always want Indian tennis to do well. Never a question.”
Article Summary: India’s top-ranked singles player Sumit Nagal has had a difficult 2026 season, with injuries disrupting his progress. The 29-year-old says he has changed his mindset and is now focused more on enjoying tennis than constantly worrying about results. Nagal won a Challenger title in Romania and reached another semifinal in Czechia.

Article Title: Mohammad Rizwan loses Lahore HC plea; PCB to take actions on Pakistan cricketers

PCB to decide next step

The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) is waiting for the findings of a National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) probe before deciding whether to take disciplinary action against senior players Mohammad Rizwan and Imam-ul-Haq The development comes after the Lahore High Court dismissed Rizwan’s petition challenging the notices issued to him by the NCCIA. Chief Justice Aalia Neelum rejected the petition during Thursday’s hearing after hearing arguments from both sides.Rizwan’s lawyer, Qazi Umair Ali, told the court that his client had been issued notices. The chief justice advised the player to respond to them."You should go and respond to the notice. On which date was the notice issued to you?" Chief Justice Neelum remarked, as quoted by news agency PTI.The lawyer claimed that Rizwan was questioned at a hotel after the Lord’s Test without being given a notice and that his mobile phone was taken.He said Rizwan had handed over the phone after being told it would be returned within three hours, but it had still not been returned.Rizwan’s lawyer also questioned the NCCIA’s authority to investigate the matter. He argued that the ICC Anti-Corruption Unit was the appropriate body to deal with corruption-related concerns involving cricketers and said the case had not been referred to the ICC unit.Rizwan had challenged the NCCIA summons in court, questioning both the agency’s jurisdiction and the nature of the investigation.Meanwhile, the NCCIA is conducting a forensic examination of mobile phones taken from Rizwan and Imam, according to PTI source familiar with the developments. The agency is expected to submit its findings to the PCB next week.“How the PCB decides to move against the two players will now depend on what findings the NCCIA submits to the PCB. If nothing out of the ordinary is found in the forensics examination they will probably get reprieves,” the source said.The PCB’s decision on possible disciplinary action will depend on the NCCIA report. The board is expected to assess the findings before deciding whether any action is required against the two players.For now, the focus remains on the forensic examination of the phones and the report that the NCCIA is expected to submit to the PCB.
Article Summary: Mohammad Rizwan and Imam-ul-Haq are being investigated by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency. The Pakistan Cricket Board is waiting for the findings of the NCCIA probe before deciding whether to take disciplinary action. The Lahore High Court dismissed Rizwana’s petition challenging the notices issued to him by the agency.

MUMBAI: Amid growing calls for a leadership change in Indian women’s cricket, former India captain Anjum Chopra has backed Harmanpreet Kaur to continue leading the side, insisting she remains the best person for the job despite recent scrutiny over her form.Harmanpreet scored 71 runs in five matches at the Women’s T20 Asia Cup in Dubai, where India lifted a record-extending eighth title. With the skipper now 37 and vice-captain Smriti Mandhana 30, suggestions of a transition in leadership have gathered momentum.Chopra, however, believes Harmanpreet remains India’s best captain. “People keep talking about changing the captain, but somebody has to lead every Indian team. As of now, Harmanpreet is the best captain to lead India,” Chopra told TOI.While acknowledging that Harmanpreet’s batting in Dubai fell below expectations, Chopra warned against judging the veteran solely on recent returns. “We always expect a special innings from her, something that reminds us of the 171 not out she scored against Australia in the 2017 World Cup. But that won’t happen every time,” she said.Chopra is confident the experienced batter will rediscover her rhythm as India build towards the inaugural Women’s Champions Trophy in 2027.“She knows fluency with the bat will be important going into major tournaments. The upcoming assignments, including the Asian Games and future bilateral series, will help her get there. She may be on the other side of 30, but India still need her services as captain and batter,” Chopra said.Fresh from an unbeaten Asia Cup campaign, India enter the Asian Games in Japan as defending champions and overwhelming favourites. Chopra believes adapting quickly to unfamiliar conditions will be their biggest challenge.“Understanding the pitches, environment and playing conditions will be crucial. On paper, India have a stronger side than the other Asian teams, but no tournament can be taken lightly. If they adapt well and play to their strengths, they should start as favourites,” she said.Chopra also praised Shafali Verma, who topped the scoring charts at the Asia Cup with 236 runs at a strike rate of 171.01 and three half-centuries.(Watch the Asian Games 2026 live and exclusive on Sony Sports Network and Sony LIV.)

Chopra is confident the experienced batter will rediscover her rhythm as India build towards the inaugural Women's Champions Trophy in 2027. India enter the Asian Games in Japan as defending champions and overwhelming favourites.

Pakistan captain Babar Azam is set to return to domestic first-class cricket for the first time in nearly seven years, with the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) keen to see him back in action following Pakistan’s disappointing Test tour of England.Babar to represent Oil and Gas Development Company Limited (OGDCL) against Kingsmen Academy in the ongoing President’s Trophy Grade-I competition, starting September 18. His return comes after Pakistan suffered a 0-3 series whitewash in England and the PCB made sweeping changes to the touring squad and coaching staff.Babar has not played domestic first-class cricket since 2019, when he represented Central Punjab in the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy. OGDCL sports head Farah Batool said the PCB had sent his name to the team for inclusion as a guest player.“Babar’s kit has been ordered and he will decide whether to play in the match from September 18 or from September 24 in the third-round game,” Batool said.Babar is not the only centrally contracted Pakistan player featuring in domestic red-ball cricket after the England tour. Haris, who has played only one Test, against England in 2022, when he suffered an injury after bowling 13 overs, has expressed his willingness to return to Pakistan’s Test setup.“If I can be useful for Pakistan because of my pace, I would gladly play Test cricket,” he said.The fast bowler, who is primarily known for his T20 performances, had declined to play the Test series in Australia in December 2023, citing the need to manage his workload. His central contract was also suspended for a period before being restored.Babar was reappointed Pakistan’s Test captain in July and has since overseen a 1-1 series draw against the West Indies and a 0-3 defeat to England. The PCB’s decision to make seven changes to the squad and remove head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul after the second Test at Lord’s reportedly came without consulting or informing Babar.Pakistan’s defeat in the second Test came inside three days, prompting major changes ahead of the final match of the series.

Article Title: Pakistan dressing-room leaks: No significant evidence recovered from Mohammed Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq's phones, but investigation still on

NCCIA continues probe into alleged Pakistan dressing-room leaks

Rizwan, Imam questioned over contacts and activities in England

Pakistan cricketers Mohammad Rizwan and Imam-ul-Haq have received some initial relief in the ongoing investigation into alleged dressing-room leaks, with the examination of their mobile phones reportedly failing to uncover any significant evidence. However, the inquiry by Pakistan’s National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) remains ongoing, with investigators continuing to examine digital records and financial transactions linked to the two players.According to Geo News, the initial examination of the phones did not reveal anything significant, although further forensic analysis is still underway at the NCCIA headquarters in Islamabad.The investigation was initiated following concerns over alleged leaks of sensitive information from the Pakistan dressing room. The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) had reportedly handed over the players’ mobile phones to the authorities for examination.According to sources cited by Geo News, the PCB took custody of Rizwan and Imam’s mobile phones before handing them over to the relevant authorities for examination. Investigators have been reviewing messages, contacts and other digital information retrieved from the devices. Information circulating on social media regarding alleged leaks from the Pakistan dressing room is also understood to be part of the inquiry.While the initial examination did not uncover anything significant, the forensic analysis is continuing. The investigation is also looking into the players’ financial dealings, with authorities reportedly reviewing their bank accounts and transactions from before and after Pakistan’s England tour. Investigators are expected to trace the source and destination of funds if any suspicious transactions are identified.Rizwan and Imam appeared before the NCCIA in Lahore earlier this month, where they were questioned about the alleged leaks. Sources said the investigators also asked the two cricketers about their contacts and meetings during practice sessions and matches in England.Both players reportedly sought additional time to submit detailed written responses to the questions raised by the authorities. Meanwhile, Rizwan has submitted a written response to the NCCIA, seeking clarification about the reasons for his summons and asking why his mobile phone has not yet been returned.The NCCIA is expected to submit its findings to PCB officials once the forensic examination is completed. According to Geo News, the PCB will decide on the matter involving the two players in light of the agency’s reportThe PCB has previously said it would not comment on the ongoing inquiry. No final findings have been announced, and the allegations against Rizwan and Imam remain under investigation.
Article Summary: Pakistan cricketers Mohammad Rizwan and Imam-ul-Haq have received some initial relief in the ongoing investigation into alleged dressing-room leaks. The examination of their mobile phones reportedly failed to uncover any significant evidence. The inquiry by Pakistan’s National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) remains ongoing.

Article Title: IPL chairman Arun Dhumal confirms push to bring 2027 auction back to India

IPL 2027 auction : BCCI keen to bring event back to India

Impact Player rule back under discussion ahead of IPL 2027

The IPL could witness two significant developments ahead of the 2027 season, with the player auction likely to return to India after three years overseas and the future of the Impact Player rule back under discussion. IPL chairman Arun Dhumal has expressed his desire to bring the auction back home, while the BCCI is seeking fresh feedback from franchises and other stakeholders on the controversial substitution rule.The auction for the 2027 season is expected to be a smaller event, with the host city yet to be finalised. The previous three editions were held outside India, in Dubai, Jeddah and Abu Dhabi. Dhumal, who is set to be re-elected as IPL chairman at the BCCI Annual General Meeting on September 18, said the league would make another attempt to host the auction in India.The IPL auction has been held overseas for the past three years, with Dubai hosting the 2024 auction, Jeddah staging the 2025 mega auction and Abu Dhabi hosting the 2026 auction. Dhumal said the league had been trying to bring the event back to India but faced difficulties in securing a suitable venue due to the busy wedding season."Every year we try for this to happen in India, but we don't get the venue given the heavy marriage season.So, we definitely want it to be here this year, given that it would be a smaller auction and hopefully we will get the venue," Dhumal told PTI.The host city for the auction will be decided based on the availability of the BCCI's preferred venue.The future of the Impact Player rule has also emerged as a key talking point ahead of the 2027 season, with the BCCI seeking fresh feedback from franchises. The matter was discussed at a recent IPL Governing Council meeting after the board approached teams for their views on the rule, which is currently scheduled to remain in place until 2027.Several prominent Indian cricketers, including Test and ODI captain Shubman Gill, former India captain Rohit Sharma, Hardik Pandya and Axar Patel, have expressed reservations about the rule. One of the key concerns raised by players is that it reduces the importance of all-rounders by allowing teams to bring in a specialist batter or bowler during a match.Ahead of IPL 2026, several captains had conveyed their concerns to the BCCI, renewing calls for the rule to be scrapped. Dhumal said the board was open to reviewing the concept but would consult all stakeholders before making a decision."The matter is under discussion. Will take a feedback from all the stakeholders and then take a call on this," he said.The Impact Player rule allows teams to substitute a player at any stage of a match, giving them the flexibility to bring in an additional batter or bowler depending on the match situation.
Article Summary: IPL chairman Arun Dhumal keen to bring event back to India. Impact Player rule back under discussion ahead of IPL 2027 season. Previous three editions were held outside India, in Dubai, Jeddah and Abu Dhabi. Host city will be decided based on availability of the BCCI's preferred venue.

India's preparations for the 2027 ODI World Cup have already brought one major question into focus: what will their squad look like when the tournament gets underway in October?The World Cup will be staged in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, with India aiming to win the title for the third time after falling short in the 2023 final. With Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli having retired from the other formats of international cricket, their availability for the 50-over showpiece remains a key talking point.Amid the uncertainty, India's 2011 World Cup hero Yuvraj Singh has stressed the importance of one thing above all else: consistency.Speaking to Cricinfo, Yuvraj said India should settle on a core group of 16 to 20 players and give them regular opportunities in the limited number of ODIs available before the World Cup."They need to focus on building the same team to play in a year's time, because you don't want to make big changes at the last moment," Yuvraj Singh said.The former all-rounder believes regular game time will be particularly important with the ODI calendar becoming increasingly limited compared to T20 cricket."Whoever your players are, whether they are 16 or 20, it's important that everybody gets game time because obviously now there are more T20S and less 50-over cricket. Whatever matches there are, it's important that players get enough game time to prepare for the World Cup," he added.Yuvraj pointed to India's past struggles at major tournaments and argued that sudden changes close to a World Cup can disrupt a team's preparations."Every time India has faltered is when they've made some massive changes at the last moment or in the tournament. So I think it's important that we stick to a team that we believe can lift the 2027 World Cup and stick by those guys whether they fail or succeed till that moment.Belief in the squad is very important," Yuvraj further said.He also cited India's success in the 2024 and 2026 T20 World Cups as an example of how developing a settled group can help a team prepare for a major tournament. India also reached the 50-over World Cup final in 2023."That's something that we have also done in the last two T20 World Cups," Yuvraj said. "We also played the 50-over World Cup final [in 2023]. So we have had a lot of consistency in white-ball cricket. And that's what they need to do as well, to think of first qualifying for the semis and then going on to play in the last two [knockout matches]. I think that's a long way ahead. Focus should be on getting a squad ready, which is together and ready to fight in any situation," the star former all-rounder further went on to say.
Article Summary: India preparing for 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli have retired from other formats of international cricket. Yuvraj Singh says India should settle on a core group of 16 to 20 players.

Article Title: Rajasthan stuck in 2012, Manipur in 2023: How actively are states with CWG medals promoting sports?
Article Text:
Are sports bodies of Indian states promoting the game properly?

Manipur still talking about 2023

Rajasthan: 14 years and counting

The ones somewhere in the middle

Does it matter so much?

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is more important for grassroots sports promotion? Social media presence Local sports events Government funding 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Somewhere on a muddy school field in Haryana right now, a teenager is perhaps drilling the same throwing technique over and over, just as she had watched on television just days ago. Her sole aim is to pull off the one like Sharmila Dhankar, India's Commonwealth Games shot put gold medallist.Before the 2026 CWG campaign, she, like many of us, had almost certainly never heard the name. And it's not because Dhankar had not won anything before the Glasgow Games; she had, a gold medal in the Women's Shot Put F57 event at the 2026 Fazza International Para Athletics Championship, but because one of the primary institutions whose entire job was to carry that story back from the medal podium to villages and training grounds across the state has, for all practical purposes, gone quiet.That's the part of this story that rarely gets told. India walked away from Glasgow with 39 medals, and for a week, the athletes who won them were everywhere, garlanded at airports, seated beside ministers, their faces on the evening news. But medals don't build the next generation of athletes by themselves. Somebody has to keep telling their stories, long after the felicitation photo is filed away, to the kid training in a dusty school ground who needs proof that this path actually leads somewhere.We wanted to know which state sports departments are still doing their job of promoting the sports and their grassroots on their social media platforms, and which ones seem to have simply logged off. So we scrolled through the timelines ourselves. Here's what we found.No state produced more glory in Glasgow than Haryana. Eleven medallists, including seven gold, two silver, two bronze, spanning boxing, wrestling, athletics, and para sport, headlined by a Neeraj Chopra silver that will be replayed on sports channels for years.Alongside him were names most of India still had little knowledge of. The likes of Preeti Pawar, Jaismine Lamboria, Sakshi Chaudhary, Priya Ghanghas, Sachin Siwach, and Ankush Panghal, all of whom trained in government facilities, under government schemes, and who'd probably appreciate their own state department cheering as loudly for them as it does for its concert lineups.Because that's the thing. The Sports Department, Government of Haryana's X account has posted exactly once in all of 2026, and it's a flyer for the music acts playing at the Chief Minister's Cup.Facebook and Instagram follow a similar rhythm with a short cluster of posts around that February event, and then not much else.Eleven medals, and not one dedicated post to show for it. Somewhere in Rohtak or Bhiwani, a young pugilist training in Priya Ghanghas's discipline would probably just like a little proof that someone up top is paying attention.Manipur's page has an odd time-capsule quality to it. This is the state that gave India Mirabai Chanu, one of the country's most beloved Olympic medalists, and this Commonwealth Games alone produced four medalists from Manipur, Chanu's gold among them, alongside Rishikanta Singh, Bindyarani Devi, and Jadumani Singh.And yet the Department of Youth Affairs & Sports' X account hasn't posted since October 2023, a "Run for Unity" event, frozen well before any of this year's medals happened.Although the Facebook page has had a few sporadic posts here and there this year, its Instagram account has managed just two posts since January. It’s the kind of gap that makes you wonder if someone simply forgot the login details somewhere along the way.If there's one number in this whole exercise worth sitting with, it's this: the official Sports Department, Government of Rajasthan hasn't posted on Facebook since April 14, 2012.Fourteen years, through Arundhati Choudhary's Commonwealth gold and everything else that's happened in Rajasthan sport since.Its X account's last original post predates a retweet from March 2021, and there's no Instagram at all. A parallel handle, the Rajasthan State Sports Council, exists across all three platforms and is barely livelier.Somewhere behind Choudhary's medal is a genuinely good story, but it just hasn't found a home on the one page built to tell it.Gulveer Singh managed both a silver and a bronze for Uttar Pradesh this Games, a rare double that would make a great centrepiece for the state's sporting year. Instead, across two separate official handles on three platforms, Uttar Pradesh Sports has produced little beyond reposts, while its sister account, Sports Directorate, Govt of Uttar Pradesh, hasn't posted at all in 2026.Delhi Government, for its part, doesn't run a dedicated sports account at all on any of the popular social media platforms, so gold medalist Harsh Singh and bronze medalist Tejaswin Shankar, both representing India's capital, don't really have an institutional cheerleader online, their wins quietly absorbed into the general churn of city government updates. Both athletes are, in effect, doing their own promotional legwork.Set against all that quiet, Tamil Nadu feels like a different sport altogether. Its Sports Tamil Nadu handles post multiple times a day, celebrating not just its own three medalists, Praveen Chithravel, Selva Prabhu, Muthupandi Raja, but athletes from other states too, weaving in government scheme updates without it ever reading like bureaucracy.Every medallist got a dedicated post. Somewhere in Tamil Nadu, a kid training in long jump or wrestling doesn't have to wonder whether the sport leads anywhere. The state tells them, publicly, almost daily.Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka's Facebook and Instagram pages, Assam, Bihar, and Tripura all follow a version of that same habit, active, consistent, generous with attention toward athletes nobody outside their district would otherwise know existed.Kerala doesn't run a separate sports handle on X but keeps its Facebook and Instagram genuinely lively, making sure Murali Sreeshankar and Mohammed Basil's silvers got their due.Andhra Pradesh mirrors that same rhythm across all three platforms.Not every state falls neatly into being inactive or staying proactive. Punjab's account managed just two posts on X all year, New Year's and Republic Day, though its Facebook and Instagram carry a bit more life around coaching and departmental meetings, even if athletes rarely get top billing.Uttarakhand was genuinely active last year before cooling off in 2026, leaning more toward government scheme announcements on Facebook, though its Instagram at least carried two posts around the Games.Maharashtra has dedicated posts up for both Sarvesh Kushare and Dilip Gavit, with Instagram staying fairly regular, enough effort to stay out of the quiet column.Karnataka's X account hasn't posted since March 2024, around an unrelated cultural-team event, even though its Facebook and Instagram have stayed warm and active toward its CWG medalists.It is worth asking why this actually matters, beyond good manners. Well, a state sports department's social media feed isn't just a courtesy board for congratulations; it's one of the cheapest, most direct tools available to build the next generation of athletes.A youngster in a small town is far more likely to pick up a javelin because they saw a state government post celebrating someone from their own district. Even when it comes to promoting any government policy, social media can be as effective.Visibility drives aspiration. There's a funding logic too. Sponsors, corporates, and even state finance departments allocate resources partly based on visible public interest, and a well-run social account is often the easiest evidence a sport has that interest.ALSO READ: Anahat Singh: What is in the name? A word from Guru Nanak's prayer, now India's squash sensation Silence, on the other hand, sends the message that grassroots sport isn't a priority worth the effort of a single post, even when the state has just produced a medallist on the world stage.It is worth it because sometimes, the first step towards building a sporting culture is simply showing people that their achievements are being seen.
Article Summary: India won 39 medals at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Haryana produced 11 medallists, including seven gold, two silver, two bronze. But the state sports department has posted just once in all of 2026. What do you think is more important for grassroots sports promotion? Government funding or social media presence? Share your view.

Article Title: ‘That video was not ordinary’: PM Modi praises Lovlina for objecting to distorted India map - Watch
Article Text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi shares a light moment with boxer Lovlina Borgohain. (PTI Photo)

‘That video was not ordinary’

Mirabai opens up about four difficult years

Narender's joke leaves Modi laughing

NEW DELHI: Boxer Lovlina Borgohain's decision to object to a distorted Indian map during the Commonwealth Games earned special appreciation from Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who described the moment as one that would be remembered for a long time.Lovlina, who won silver in the women's 75kg category in Glasgow, was among India's medal winners who interacted with Modi at his residence on Sunday. The meeting, attended by Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya, Minister of State for Sports Raksha Khadse and Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha, saw athletes recount their experiences from the Games in an informal and emotional setting.In a little over 10-minute video of the interaction shared by the Prime Minister's Office on Monday, Modi brought up Lovlina's confrontation with a restaurant in Glasgow after she noticed a distorted Indian map.“Kya hua wo restaurant waale se jhagda kar rahi thi? (What happened, you were fighting with that restaurant guy?)” Modi asked.Lovlina laughed before explaining why she intervened.“We had such a good performance and it was the last day of the Games. It was a happy occasion sir, we were celebrating and I didn't like it when I saw the distorted map. I politely told them and they have made the changes also,” she explained.Modi applauded the boxer for noticing the issue despite being in the middle of celebrations after her medal-winning campaign.“To be able to recognise the significance of that map at a time when you were celebrating and the Games were over, I can tell you truthfully, that video was not ordinary. It will be remembered by people for a very long time,” he told the Tokyo Olympics bronze medallist.India finished fourth in Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 golds, with boxing contributing seven gold medals.The interaction also provided an emotional window into Mirabai Chanu's journey to her gold medal in the women's 48kg category. The weightlifter produced a Games-record lift of 190kg, but her triumph came after four difficult years following her one-kilogram miss at the Paris Olympics. Modi asked Mirabai about the tears she shed on the podium and even fed her a laddu during their interaction.“Itne aansu tapak rahe the (So many tears were rolling down),” Modi remarked.Mirabai explained that the tears represented years of accumulated emotions.“I was very happy and emotional at that moment. I was crying because I missed a medal in the Paris Olympics by one kilogram. I have faced a lot in these last four years. I was battling injuries and some family problems too.“There were a lot of things. So, these four years were very tough for me. And when I stood on the podium, our flag went up and the anthem played, it was hard to stop myself,” she said.The meeting also had its lighter moments. Boxer Narender Berwal, who won silver in the +90kg category, recalled a funny exchange with a Pakistani boxer after beating him at the 2015 World Military Games.“During the 2015 World Military Games, I had a bout with a Pakistani boxer. I won it but when we were together in the medical room for treatment to our niggles, he said to me 'Bhaijan aapka naam Narender hai, aapke coach ka naam Narender hai, aapke Pradhan Mantri ka naam Narender hai, mujhe Narender naam se nafrat ho gayi hai.' (Brother, you, your coach and your PM are all named Narender. I hate this name now),” he recalled, drawing laughter from Modi.The Prime Minister also underlined the broader significance of the athletes' achievements, saying their medals were helping inspire a new generation.“I have been in this house for 12-13 years now and if there is one group that I have met regularly here, it is the athletes because of your efforts to win medals for India and your tradition of scaling new heights.“Far more than our push to promote sports in schools, it is your medals that inspire people,” Modi said.
Article Summary: Lovlina Borgohain won silver in the women's 75kg category in Glasgow. Prime Minister Narendra Modi described the moment as one that would be remembered for a long time. India finished fourth in Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 golds, with boxing contributing seven gold medals.

Article Title: ‘From every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping’: PM Modi’s heartfelt message to CWG heroes - Watch
Article Text:
PM Narendra Modi interacted with India's CWG 2026 medal winners at his residence on Sunday. (Pic credit: PM Modi's X post)

NEW DELHI: “From every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping.”Prime Minister Narendra Modi had an emotional message for Mirabai Chanu as he interacted with India's Commonwealth Games 2026 medal winners at his residence on Sunday, reflecting on the sacrifices behind the country's successful campaign in Glasgow.Modi hosted the medal-winning contingent at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg and heard athletes recount some of the moments that defined their journeys at the Games. India returned from Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze, finishing fourth in the overall standings.During one of the conversations, Modi recalled the emotional scenes surrounding Mirabai's gold-medal triumph.“Tears were falling from you. I feel as if from every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping,” Modi told the Olympic silver medallist.Mirabai, who won gold in Glasgow, opened up about the difficult journey that preceded her Commonwealth Games triumph, including the disappointment of the Paris Olympics.“I was very happy, and emotional too. That day the happiness was greater and I cried because at the Paris Olympics, I lost a medal by 1 kg. In a player’s life what all we have to face. So within these 4 years, how much and what all I had faced, every time injuries were going on and all that was happening.So with great difficulty I had faced these 4 years. So when all that happened, on the podium when I stood, sir, and when our flag goes up and our national anthem plays, sir, we cannot stop, sir, tears come out on their own,” she said.Modi responded by highlighting the wider impact of the athletes' achievements.“This is very good. It is not as if this achievement of yours is considered only your achievement; your victory becomes a very big inspiration for the coming generations.”The informal interaction also saw athletes share lighter and deeply personal moments from their Glasgow campaigns.Modi reminded para shot put gold medallist Sharmila Dhankar of a promise she had made earlier.“You made a promise. Last time, yours, both daughters will become players,” Modi said with a smile.Dhankar replied: “Haanji, right now they are young in age. In the next Commonwealth, one family will bring 3 medals.”Men's 100m T47 gold medallist Dilip Gavit, meanwhile, spoke about dedicating his performance to his guru.“When I was running, when my event was on 29th (July), that day was Guru Purnima, so that day I gave a gift to my guru,” he was heard saying in the video.In another video posted by Modi, gold medallist boxer Sakshi Chaudhary introduced herself and the contingent.“Hello friends! This is Sakshi Chaudhary. Today, our honourable Prime Minister has invited us, the Commonwealth Games medalists, and we feel very proud. We are extremely happy to have met him; he is very humble. Sir, would you like to say something?” she said.Modi replied with a message that summed up his interaction with the athletes: “Jo khelega, woh khilega” (The one who plays, will blossom). “Always cheer for Bharat.”India's fourth-place finish came despite a significantly smaller contingent and a reduced sporting programme compared to Birmingham 2022. India sent 122 athletes to Glasgow, compared to 210 in Birmingham, while 30 of its 61 medals in 2022 came in sports that were not part of the Glasgow programme.Despite those limitations, India retained its fourth-place position and improved its medal conversion rate, with 38 athletes returning home with medals. Long-distance runner Gulveer Singh was the only Indian athlete to win two medals.The Glasgow Games concluded after 11 days, with Scotland handing over the Commonwealth Games flag and ceremonial baton to India ahead of the 2030 edition in Ahmedabad.The symbols were handed to Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra, Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha and Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi during the closing ceremony.Ahmedabad will become only the second Indian city to host the Commonwealth Games after New Delhi staged the 2010 edition.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi hosted medal-winning contingent at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg. Modi heard athletes recount some of the moments that defined their journeys. India returned from Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze.
